subject: Help for a complex multilevel moderated mediation

messages.author: ce11a6290780d3ae
messages.subject: Help for a complex multilevel moderated mediation
parts:
Dear all,

I am working on a multilevel moderated mediation and I decided to use the lavaan package. I briefly describe the data I have (I added also the dataframe):

- time: one categorical predictor (two levels)
- memory task: continuous dependent variable,
- anxiety and depression: continuous mediators
- age: continuous moderator
- group: categorical moderator (three levels)

I attach the general model I would like to test (upper path diagram), also with the path coefficients (lower path diagram):



It is possible to generate them by using the folowing code:
library(processR)
labels=list(X="Time",M=c("Anx","Dep"),Y="Y")
moderator=list(name=c("Age","Group_cat1","Group_cat2"),
               matrix=list(c(1,1,0,1,1,1),c(0,0,0,0,1,1),c(0,0,0,0,1,1)),
               pos=c(1,2,4))

drawConcept(labels=labels,parallel=TRUE,moderator=moderator)
drawModel(labels=labels,parallel=TRUE,moderator=moderator,drawbox = F)

As far I can understand, a way to deal with categorical data is to convert them into dummy coded (0/1) variables. If the variable has k levels, it is possible to create k-1 dummy coded variables OR it could be performed a multigroup analysis. I tried to apply the first way for the "Group" moderator (taking Group B as reference for both comparisons). I attach the formula I would like to pass to lavaan:

eq='
Anx~a1*Time+a2*Age+a3*Time:Age
Dep~a4*Time+a5*Age+a6*Time:Age
Y~b1*Anx+b2*Age+b3*Anx:Age+b4*Group_cat1+b5*Anx:Group_cat1+b6*Group_cat2+b7*Anx:Group_cat2+b8*Dep+b9*Dep:Age+b10*Dep:Group_cat1+b11*Dep:Group_cat2+c1*Time+c2*Age+c3*Time:Age
Age ~ Age.mean*1
Age ~~ Age.var*Age

Group_cat1 ~ Group_cat1.mean*1
Group_cat1 ~~ Group_cat1.var*Group_cat1

Group_cat2 ~ Group_cat2.mean*1
Group_cat2 ~~ Group_cat2.var*Group_cat2


# Indirect Effect(s)

indirect1 := (a1+a3*Age.mean)*(b1+b3*Age.mean+b5*Group_cat1.mean+b7*Group_cat2.mean)
direct1 :=c1+c3*Age.mean
indirect1.below :=(a1+a3*(Age.mean-sqrt(Age.var)))*(b1+b3*(Age.mean-sqrt(Age.var))+b5*(Group_cat1.mean-sqrt(Group_cat1.var))+b7*(Group_cat2.mean-sqrt(Group_cat2.var)))
indirect1.above :=(a1+a3*(Age.mean+sqrt(Age.var)))*(b1+b3*(Age.mean+sqrt(Age.var))+b5*(Group_cat1.mean+sqrt(Group_cat1.var))+b7*(Group_cat2.mean+sqrt(Group_cat2.var)))
direct1.below:=c1+c3*(Age.mean-sqrt(Age.var))
direct1.above:=c1+c3*(Age.mean+sqrt(Age.var))
total1.below := direct1.below + indirect1.below
total1.above := direct1.above + indirect1.above
prop.mediated1.below := indirect1.below / total1.below
prop.mediated1.above := indirect1.above / total1.above

indirect2 := (a4+a6*Age.mean)*(b8+b9*Age.mean+b10*Group_cat1.mean+b11*Group_cat2.mean)
direct2 :=c1+c3*Age.mean
indirect2.below :=(a4+a6*(Age.mean-sqrt(Age.var)))*(b8+b9*(Age.mean-sqrt(Age.var))+b10*(Group_cat1.mean-sqrt(Group_cat1.var))+b11*(Group_cat2.mean-sqrt(Group_cat2.var)))
indirect2.above :=(a4+a6*(Age.mean+sqrt(Age.var)))*(b8+b9*(Age.mean+sqrt(Age.var))+b10*(Group_cat1.mean+sqrt(Group_cat1.var))+b11*(Group_cat2.mean+sqrt(Group_cat2.var)))
direct2.below:=c1+c3*(Age.mean-sqrt(Age.var))
direct2.above:=c1+c3*(Age.mean+sqrt(Age.var))
total2.below := direct2.below + indirect2.below
total2.above := direct2.above + indirect2.above
prop.mediated2.below := indirect2.below / total2.below
prop.mediated2.above := indirect2.above / total2.above


# Specific Indirect Effect Contrast(s)

Contrast1 := indirect1-indirect2

# Indirect/Direct/Total Effect(s)

indirect := indirect1+indirect2
direct := c1+c3*Age.mean
total := indirect + direct
prop.mediated := indirect / total
'

mymodel=sem(model=eq,data = df)
summary( mymodel )


In other words, I would like understand if the average time differences in Y are mediated by anx and dep scores and if this effect is moderated by the age of the respondents. Furthermore, I would like to understand if there is a moderation of the groups on the path between the mediators and Y.

First issue: Am I treating correctly the categotical variables? 

Second issue: I would like to convert this model SEM (if correctly written) into a multilevel one, since this is a repeated measure design. I am completely stuck on how to code the within/random part of the model. If I used a linear mixed effect model, I would set the ID as clustering variable and random intercepts and slopes (time|ID maybe). 

I am sorry for the long post. Could you give me some help on how to rewrite my eq formula in multilevel term? Every suggestion would be precious.

Thank you in advance for your time and availability 

Best Regards,

Umberto
